# U1 pad field — VISUAL REVIEW result (gpt-6-astra)

**Artefact reviewed:** `docs/fab/reviews/u1-pad-field.png`
**Generated by:** `tracker/hardware/render_u1_pad_field.py`
**Served model:** `gpt-6-astra` (verified from the response, not the request alias)

## Why this review was run at all

`pad_audit.py` reports pad numbers — exact, but static. It can say *"13 pads share the number 41 at 13
distinct positions"* and *"9 pads have no number and no net"*. It **cannot** say whether those thirteen
sit somewhere electrically meaningful. **That is a SPATIAL question, and it is the one thing the visual
consultant is for.** This was asked as a specific, answerable question about a to-scale render, not as
"does this look right?".

## The question asked

> (1) Are the unnamed pads interleaved within the ground cluster, or spatially separate?
> (2) Do they sit in a regular pattern?
> (3) Is the 3.9 mm thermal pad at the centre?
> (4) Which is closer to U4?

## The answer, verbatim

> **1. Interleaved within the ground cluster, not spatially separate.** All nine dark-red pads lie inside
> the outline of the large orange thermal pad. The smaller orange pads occupy positions between adjacent
> dark-red pads, both horizontally and vertically.
>
> **2. A repeated 3 × 3 square grid.** The unnamed pads form three equally spaced columns and three
> equally spaced rows: top-left through bottom-right, including the centre. From the 3.9 mm thermal-pad
> scale, their centre-to-centre pitch is approximately **1.4 mm** in both directions. Relative to the
> thermal-pad centre, their centres are at every combination of horizontal and vertical offsets
> **−1.4, 0, +1.4 mm**. The twelve smaller orange ground pads sit midway between horizontally or
> vertically adjacent grid positions. This is consistent with an intentional repeated layout, though the
> image alone cannot establish why the pad numbers/nets are missing.
>
> **3. Yes.** The 3.9 mm orange thermal pad is centred on the orange group and spans the entire array.
> Its centre coincides with the centre dark-red pad.
>
> **4. Cannot determine from this image.** No blue-circled U4 radio or U4 position is shown. The unnamed
> array and ground cluster share a centre; neither forms a separate group displaced toward U4. **A
> direction or distance comparison to U4 requires its position.**

## What this CHANGES in the diagnosis

**The earlier written diagnosis was wrong about the nature of the nine pads**, and this review corrects
it:

| earlier text | what the measurement plus this review show |
|---|---|
| "nine unnamed pads at distinct positions — floating copper, a real electrical gap" | **a deliberate 3 × 3 via array inside the thermal pad, unfinished.** Regular 1.4 mm pitch at exactly −1.4/0/+1.4 mm offsets is design intent, not corruption |
| "the 3 × 3 grid of small ground pads plus the central thermal pad is the signature of a footprint built by replicating a pad without renumbering" | **the twelve small pads are the ring at the MIDPOINTS between via positions**, i.e. they are a separate, correctly-numbered feature; the `41` collision is a *numbering* fault, not the same fault as the unnamed pads |

**So the two defects are distinct in kind, not two symptoms of one mistake:**

1. **The twelve + one pads all numbered `41`** — a **numbering** fault. KiCad cannot address them
   separately, so no tool can refer to an individual one.
2. **The nine unnamed pads on no net** — almost certainly the **thermal vias** for the ESP32's exposed
   pad. They carry no number and no net, so **they do not connect the module's thermal pad to the ground
   plane.** That is a real thermal and electrical consequence, and it is now *explainable* rather than
   mysterious.

**The physical reading that fits both:** this footprint appears to have been assembled from a base pad
pattern (numbering carried over, hence the repeated `41`) plus a via field that was placed but never
given numbers and nets.

## The consultant refused question 4, and that is the correct behaviour

U4's marker was drawn only if it fell inside the canvas, and it fell outside. **The consultant said
"cannot determine" and named exactly what it would need** — *"a direction or distance comparison to U4
requires its position"* — rather than inventing an answer.

**That is the same discipline the ERC, DRC, model-census and determinism gates use: a check that cannot
answer must say so.** It is recorded here because it is the behaviour the rest of this work keeps failing
to show.

## Follow-up worth running

Re-render with **U4's marker guaranteed inside the frame** (widen the canvas or draw a leader to an
off-canvas arrow), then ask the question again. `U1` is the ESP32 module and `U4` is the SX1280 radio;
whether the unfinished via field faces the radio matters for whether the thermal path also serves the RF
ground return.
